gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the YesWelder TIG-200P ACDC PRO sustains almost the same TIG current at 100% duty on 220V (110 A) as on 110V (108 A). On a 240V circuit its extra headroom is only 200 A at 30% duty, while the PrimeWeld TIG225X is rated 155 A at 100% on 240V. On 120V the two machines are rated the same: 108 A at 100%.
standout_why: I compared the two cited pages, homewelder.com/best-tig-welder-for-beginners and woodworking-projects.com/hobby-tig-welder. HomeWelder already lists YesWelder 30% @ 200A, ARCCAPTAIN 25% @ 200A, AHP 60% @ 200A (240V) and PrimeWeld's 100% figures of 108A (120V) and 155A (240V). It does not give YesWelder's own 100% figures (108A on 110V, 110A on 220V), so it never shows that 240V adds almost no sustained current on that machine, or that the YesWelder matches the PrimeWeld on 120V. It also never puts all the machines on one basis. Woodworking-projects lists only one duty figure per model, at mixed amperages (40% @ 225A, 35% @ 200A, 60% @ 190A), and does not normalise them. Neither page says the YesWelder bundle with the pedal costs less today than the bare unit.
decides: If the shopper has only 120V, YesWelder ($599.15 with pedal today) and PrimeWeld TIG225X are both rated 108 A at 100% duty. PrimeWeld's higher price then buys a CK torch, warranty and AC controls, not more sustained current, which makes YesWelder the value pick. If the shopper has 240V and will weld thicker aluminum, PrimeWeld (155 A at 100%, stated) and AHP 203Xi (about 155 A at 100%, derived) carry roughly 45 A more continuous current than YesWelder (110 A) or ARCCAPTAIN TIG200P (about 100 A, derived), which favours them. LOTOS TIG200ACDC is still the cheapest with the pedal included, but I could not source its duty cycle, so it can't be placed on this basis.
